description:
GitHub issue #142: https://github.com/jallum/beadwork/issues/142

## What happens

Every `bw` command fails immediately on a repo using git's reftable ref backend:

```
$ bw ready
error: open repo: core.repositoryformatversion does not support extension: refstorage
```

Reproduce on any git 2.45+:

```
git init --ref-format=reftable r && cd r
git commit --allow-empty -m init
bw ready
```

## Why

reftable keeps every ref in `.git/reftable/`. `.git/refs/heads/` is empty and `.git/HEAD` is the stub `ref: refs/heads/.invalid`. go-git reads `.git/refs/**` plus `packed-refs`, and `verifyExtensions` rejects `extensions.refstorage` outright.

Unlike `worktreeConfig` (#117) or negative fetch refspecs, this one is **not** safe to bypass by stripping the extension from config: go-git would then open the repo and see zero refs instead of erroring, which is worse than the current failure.

## Why I care

My team's monorepo has been migrated to reftable, so I can't use bw on it at all. Migrating back isn't available to me either:

```
$ git refs migrate --ref-format=files --dry-run
error: migrating repositories with worktrees is not supported yet
```


## Upstream, and a misleading error message

reftable support is requested upstream as [go-git#1827](https://github.com/go-git/go-git/issues/1827), open since January with no activity — so waiting for go-git seems unlikely to pay off soon.

Worth knowing when reading the error above: it blames `core.repositoryformatversion`, but the repo *is* at `repositoryformatversion = 1`, which should take a different branch in `verifyExtensions` and report `unknown extension: refstorage` instead. The wording is wrong because of [go-git#2155](https://github.com/go-git/go-git/issues/2155) — `config.Unmarshal` never reads `core.repositoryformatversion`, so `cfg.Core.RepositoryFormatVersion` is always `""` and every repo is forced down the v0 branch. Unrelated to this issue, but it makes the error misleading if you go looking at the format version.

## Possible approach

reftable changes ref storage but not object storage, so objects are unaffected. bw already shells out to git for fetch and push, so resolving and updating refs through git (`git rev-parse`, `git update-ref`) and handing hashes to go-git might be sufficient — rather than waiting on reftable support in go-git, which doesn't exist in v5.

I'm going to take a stab at a proof of concept, but it looks like a meaningfully bigger undertaking than the refspec fix, and I'd rather hear whether this is a direction you'd want before going far with it.
title: Support repos using the reftable ref backend (extensions.refstorage=reftable)
